summary.headline: Kalyani Forge Q1 FY27 PAT rose 218% YoY to ₹4.48 crore, with EBITDA margin at an all-time high of 16.2%.
summary.overview: Revenue (total income) reached ₹67.07 crore, up 3.9% YoY and 13.2% QoQ, the highest in five-plus quarters. EBITDA rose to ₹10.89 crore at a 16.2% margin, up 640 bps YoY, driven by operating leverage, shop-floor efficiency, price increases and exits from low-margin business. Q1 PAT was normalised versus Q4, which had a one-off deferred tax gain (Q4 PAT ₹5.88 crore). Management reiterated a 20% EBITDA margin target, a capex plan of ₹30 crore for FY27 and a long-term sales CAGR aim of at least 20%.

financial_highlights.change: +3.9% YoY vs ₹64.53 crore; +13.2% QoQ vs ₹59.24 crore
+218% YoY from ₹1.41 crore; margin +450 bps YoY
Down from 168/170 days in Q4 (figures stated inconsistently; 248 days also cited once)
Newly tracked metric; all-time high in five quarters

segments.name: Engine
segments.commentary: Sales ₹40 crore vs ₹29 crore in Q1 FY26 (~38% YoY); share of sales rose from 57% to 60%. Still 60-70% of revenue per management, mainly HCV, trucks and industrial off-road.

segments.name: Axle
segments.commentary: Grew 22% YoY; management said the axle group grew substantially this quarter. Fuel-agnostic, serving passenger cars and some LCVs.

segments.name: Driveline
segments.commentary: Grew 11% YoY. Fuel-agnostic, serving passenger cars and some LCVs.

segments.name: By end market
segments.commentary: Passenger cars +35% YoY, trucks +48% YoY, industrial +67% YoY (small base), agro -31% YoY as legacy low-margin business was phased out.

segments.name: OEM revenue
segments.commentary: ₹40.7 crore, +31% YoY and +9% QoQ; fourth consecutive quarter of OEM revenue growth.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Share of sales revived to 16% from 11% in Q4; gear blanks exports to be shipped 100% machined this year versus as-forged last year.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin: sustain at 15% or more; internal target of 20% 'within a few quarters' (no firm timeline).
Revenue: no formal guidance; management expects to sustain ~₹67 crore quarterly revenue in the next several quarters.
Long-term sales CAGR: at least 20% aimed for the next five years.
Fixed asset turnover: ~2.5-2.6 now, targeting 2-2.5 near term and 2.0 over the long term.
Machining capacity to rise from 1.8 lakh to 3 lakh pieces per month by end FY27.
Wheel hub new line expected up and running by end Q2 FY27.
Vriddhi Council: ₹50 crore annual savings target; management aims to realise as much as possible within FY27.
FY27 capex plan of ₹30 crore, funded 75% debt and 25% internal accruals.
Management plans to raise equity in future (promoters to participate); no quantum given; some proceeds to repay debt.
capex_capacity: Machining capacity 1.8 lakh pieces/month at ~90-95% utilisation (conrods, wheel hubs, gear blanks, tulips); target 3 lakh/month by end FY27.
Wheel hub line: new line under installation using CNC machines redeployed from phased-out businesses; some special-purpose machinery still to be procured; expected end Q2 FY27.
Capex split ~60% to driveline/axle and ramp-up/new businesses; goals are capacity increase and OEE improvement, with tighter payback filters.
Capex in Q4 was inflated by ₹10 crore of dies and tooling reclassified from inventory to fixed assets (accounting, not cash spend).
demand_pricing: RFQ inflow continues monthly; management says it is 'a little filled up' and declining non-core RFQs. No slowdown in new business inquiries.
Wheel hubs (Gen 3, passenger cars) samples in progress, ~₹20 crore annual revenue potential; management declined to size beyond that.
Conrod share-of-wallet gains with about three customers; connecting rod growth expected through FY27.

Raw material: pass-through mechanisms with customers; price increases received for raw material and some conversion costs. Indirect material suppliers sought 15-30% hikes; some granted, with consumption controlled. OEM pricing talks still a work in progress.
Top five customers contribute ~30-40% of revenue.
Phase four of business mix optimisation (final phase): capex and capacity aligned to core customers. ~₹40 crore non-fit business phased out in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How big can the wheel hub business become, given new orders in validation?
qa_highlights.answer: Wheel hubs are used one per wheel in passenger cars, tied to PV growth; Gen 3 hubs are gaining popularity in India and replacing Gen 2/Gen 1. Management declined to give an exact number, pointing to passenger car segment growth.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Vriddhi Council work and will the ₹50 crore savings be realised in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Council is a group of project leaders running cost and productivity initiatives (material, power, manpower, pricing, VAVE, dies and tools), meeting monthly under a steering committee chaired by the MD. Savings are annualised and recur, so they spread over years; the endeavour is to get as much of ₹50 crore as possible in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ~15% EBITDA margin be sustained, when will 20% come, and what is revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will sustain 15% or more, with 20% internally targeted over coming quarters, in line with industry benchmarks; no firm timing beyond 'within a few quarters'. No formal revenue guidance, but ~₹67 crore quarterly revenue is expected to continue for several quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Fixed asset turnover outlook and five-year sales CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: Current FAT around 2.5-2.6 with fixed assets near ₹100 crore including CWIP; target 2-2.5 as capex is added and 2.0 long term. Aim for at least 20% sales CAGR over five years, based on the growth strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Why are debtors up and cash conversion days high; how will working capital be deleveraged?
qa_highlights.answer: CCC cut to 148 days from 170 last quarter, driven by reducing non-moving indirect inventory and focusing on direct material. Receivables push via structured collections, better payment terms and bill discounting; procurement budgets reset toward direct material.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vriddhi savings flow-through to P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹19 crore is an annualised figure, roughly ₹4.2 crore per quarter. Part flows directly to EBITDA; part is absorbed by inflation, wage and input cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Forging inquiry trends after the prior slowdown, and raw material pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reports no slowdown in RFQs; several arrive monthly, non-core ones are declined and the company is 'a little filled up'. Raw materials are passed through to customers; indirect material suppliers sought 15-30% hikes, some granted with consumption controlled; conversion cost pricing with OEMs still a work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive moat, top customer concentration and capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Top five customers are 30-40% of revenue. Moat cited as complex forgings with fully machined, ready-to-assemble parts and 4-5 decades of engineering. Forging capacity ~20,000 tonnes at 50-60% utilisation; machining 1.8 lakh pieces/month at 90-95%, rising to 3 lakh by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: EV risk to forging portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says engine business is mainly HCV and off-road, which has long lifecycle; driveline and axle are fuel-agnostic and serve passenger cars and LCVs. EVs seen growing mainly in two- and three-wheelers and PVs, with limited feasibility in trucks. Stub axle forging capacity is being expanded.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹30 crore FY27 capex is to be funded 75% debt and 25% internal accruals, per company policy.

risks_watch: Receivables and cash conversion: CCC cited as 148 days but also 248 days once, and debtor build-up was questioned; watch collections and bill discounting progress.
Input cost inflation: indirect material suppliers seeking 15-30% hikes and OEM conversion-cost pricing still unresolved; margin dependence on Vriddhi savings absorbing this.
EBITDA margin path: 15%+ sustain is committed, but 20% target has no firm timeline ('within a few quarters'); Q1 margin is 16.2% vs ~15% prior three quarters.
Wheel hub line: due end Q2 FY27, relies on shifting existing machines and some special-purpose machinery still to be procured; ₹20 crore potential is samples-stage.
Customer concentration: top five customers 30-40% of revenue; conrod growth depends on three customers' share-of-wallet gains.
Equity raise planned with promoter participation; no quantum or timing given; debt repayment use unquantified.
Revenue quality: Q4 PAT of ₹5.88 crore inflated by deferred tax; Q1 PAT normalised. Capex jump in Q4 partly ₹10 crore accounting reclassification; watch next-quarter comparisons.
Management says machining capacity to reach 3 lakh/month by end FY27 (from 1.8 lakh at 90-95% utilised), so capex execution is key.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 PAT is a normalised PAT and reflects the true trend of growing profitability.
We are targeting internally 20% as an EBITDA margin over the coming quarters, and this is in line with our industry benchmarks.
We do have plans to raise equity in the future.
So we would use some of the equity to repay debt, but it's too soon to state any numbers at this point.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, ROCE and new business, with the MD answering most questions directly. Cautious or non-committal on specifics: no revenue guidance, no sizing of wheel hub beyond ₹20 crore, no timeline for the 20% EBITDA margin, and no quantum or timing for the planned equity raise.
